limitations: Only integer sample sizes and iid zero-based geometric laws with 0<q<1 are covered.
Potential overlap with original exponentiated-geometric and DGEII papers could not be definitively ruled out because their complete original articles were not accessible.
scientific_integrity: The all-sample-size claim follows from a closed-form generating-function identity, an all-real-parameter induction and a convolution-root coefficient obstruction. The exact-rational checker is corroboration only. No independent audit or novelty certification is implied.
statement: For every integer \(n\ge1\) and real \(0<q<1\), the maximum of \(n\) independent zero-based geometric random variables with mass \(\Pr(X=k)=(1-q)q^k\) is infinitely divisible if and only if \(n\in\{1,2\}\). When \(n=2\), its compound-Poisson jump intensities are \(\nu_k=[q^{2k}+(1+(-1)^{k-1})q^k]/k\) for \(k\ge1\); when \(n\ge3\), the quadratic coefficient of its logarithmic probability-generating function equals \([2(1+q+q^2)^n-(1+q)^{2n}-1]/2<0\).
title: A sharp infinite-divisibility cutoff for maxima of geometric samples
